Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

18:7468-1974 




Indian Standard 



(Reaffirmed 2005) 



RECOMMENDATION ON PREFERRED STROKES 
FOR MECHANICAL AND HYDRAULIC PRESSES 



1. Scope— Prescribes preferred strokes for mechanical and iiydraulic presses. 

2. Terminology 

2.1 Stroke — The travel of the press slide between the terminal points of motion. 

3. Strokes — The preferred strokes in millimetres for mechanical and hydraulic presses shall be 
as given below: 



10 
12 
16 
20 
25 
32 
40 
50 
63 
80 
100 



125 
160 
200 
250 
315 
400 
500 
630 
800 
1000 



Note — Strokes less than 10 mm or more than 1000 mm may be chosen from RIO preferred series as given 
in IS : 1076-1967 ' Preferred numbers ( first revision )'. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard has been prepared with a view to assist the manufacturers of mechanical and 
hydraulic presses in designing new presses. Variety reduction is one of the objects aimed at for an 
organized development of any industry and it is hoped that this standard will be of help in the 
selection of strokes for mechanical and hydraulic presses within a rationalized series. 

13:7469-1974 'Recommendations on preferred capacities for mechanical and hydraulic 
presses ' is the other standard in the series of Indian Standards on parameters for presses. 



Adopted 19 November 1974 



@ February 1975, ISI
